questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

As the only ________ person in the wacky family, the sensible girl felt like the odd woman out.
questions.solution:
Answer: sane

The sentence talks about a ‘sensible’ girl, who felt like an odd one out in a wacky, i.e., crazy family. Therefore, the girl must be the only non-crazy person in the family, i.e., **sane. **Hence, the correct word to fill in the blank is sane.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Pravin sat up on the (1)/ sofa, with his legs (2)/ tucked down him. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Answer: 3

‘Tucked down’ should be replaced by ‘tucked under’ as it means draw something together in a small space.

Hence, the correct answer is ‘Pravin sat up on the sofa, with his legs tucked under him.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

The travel agent is making all the reservations.

options.text: All the reservations is made by the travel agent.
All the reserving will be made by the travel agent.
All the reservations are being made by the travel agent.
All the reserving is made by the travel agent.

questions.solution:
Answer: All the reservations are being made by the travel agent.

Sentence 1 changes the tense to the past tense, Sentence 2 changes the word ‘reservations’ and the tense and Sentence 4 does the same. Neither of the three sentences follow the tense of the Active voice, except Sentence 3 which follows the present continuous tense. Hence, the correct option is Option 3.

questions.question: so the more you do it, the ________ your stamina.
questions.solution:
Answer: better

The sentence makes a comparison, stating that the ‘more’ one does it, the stamina will improve correspondingly. Hence, we use the comparative form of ‘good’, i.e. ‘better’.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

In exactly the same words as were used originally
questions.solution:
Answer: Verbatim

Verbatim means in exactly the same words as were used originally. Hence, it is the correct one-word substitute for the given phrase.

On the other hand, offbeat means unconventional, divergent means tending to be different and contrary means opposite in nature or meaning.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

To have bitten off more than you can chew

options.text: To eat voraciously and then fall sick
To behave disrespectfully towards elders and then repent the act
To have tried to do something which is too difficult
To have missed a golden opportunity and after that willing to put twice the effort to recover the

questions.solution:
Answer: To have tried to do something which is too difficult

The phrase ‘bite off more than one can chew’ means to take on more responsibility than one can handle, i.e., to try to do something too difficult.

An example sentence is: ‘By volunteering to manage all the departments, I have bitten off more than I can chew.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

At night, the hungry orphan would sneak into the kitchen and __________ tiny amounts of food
questions.solution:
Answer: pilfer

Pilfer means to steal something, generally things of little value. Hence, it is the appropriate word to fill in the blank as it completes the meaning of the sentence. Prefer means to like something over another thing and differ means to be dissimilar.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Out of print

options.text: Not able to print due to being short on paper
A book no longer available from the publisher
Intentionally not mention some items in the article or book
All publishers refuse to publish your book

questions.solution:
Answer: A book no longer available from the publisher

The phrase ‘out of print’ means something that is no longer printed or sold by a publisher.

An example sentence is: ‘It was quite disheartening to hear that my mentor’s book had gone out of print.’

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

But this does not mean

X-phenomena to the body 

Y-is a meaningless expression 

Z-that the reference of mental
questions.solution:
Answer: ZXY

The word ‘mean’ is a verb, that is used to convey something. Therefore, it must be followed by the word ‘that’ to show reference. Only Z starts with ‘that’, therefore the passage should start with Z, as seen in Option 2 only. Hence, the correct option is ZXY.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

What would the cavalry (doing) out here?
questions.solution:
Answer: be doing

The word ‘doing’ is incorrect as it does not utilize the ‘be’ verb to denote action. The correct form is ‘be doing’, which shows the action the cavalry could be doing.

Therefore, the sentence is: ‘What would the cavalry be doing out here?’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.**

To Indict
questions.solution:
**To indict** means** to formally accuse or charge someone of a crime**.

On the other hand,** to exonerate** means** to clear someone of a blame or crime**. Hence, the two words have opposite meanings.

To censure means to express a strong disapproval, to arraign means to call someone before a court on a criminal charge and to impeach means to call into question the validity of a practice.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Water was dripping (1)/ of the trees, and (2)/ the grass was wet. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Answer: 2

‘Dripping of’ is incorrect as it does not have any meaning. The correct phrase is ‘dripping from’, meaning fall in small drops.

Hence, the correct sentence is: ‘Water was dripping from the trees, and the grass was wet.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I'm (having to) too much fun.
questions.solution:
Answer: having

The phrase in the bracket makes the sentence grammatically incorrect. ‘Having’ is the correct option since the sentence is in present continuous tense, as denoted by ‘I am’. Therefore, the sentence is: ‘I’m having too much fun.’

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.**

A person inclined to question or doubt accepted opinions
questions.solution:
Answer: Sceptic

Sceptic means a person inclined to question or doubt accepted opinions. Hence, it is the correct one-word substitute for the given phrase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Adherent**: A supporter or follower.

Example sentence: Jane is an adherent of a healthy lifestyle and exercises regularly.

**Zealot**: An extremely passionate or fanatical person.

Example sentence: The football fan was a zealot, always wearing his team's jersey and cheering loudly at matches.

**Disciple**: A follower or student of a teacher or philosophy.

Example sentence: Sarah is a disciple of yoga and practices it daily to improve her flexibility and mindfulness.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Children are sensitive

X-to what happens around them and are

Y-enthusiastic about working on

Z-plays that reflect their lives
questions.solution:
Answer: XYZ

The first sentence should be in flow with the word ‘sensitive’. Since X starts with ‘to what happens’, it is in flow and is the first sentence. Therefore, Option 3, which has X as the first sentence, is the correct option.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

He said to the dentist, "I have a toothache."

options.text: He told the dentist that I have a toothache.
He told the dentist that he had gotten a toothache.
He told the dentist that he had a toothache.
He told the dentist that I have a gotten toothache.

questions.solution:
Answer: He told the dentist that he had a toothache.

Sentence 1 does not convert the first person to third person, Sentences 2 and 4 introduce the word ‘gotten’, along with an incorrect tense usage. Only Sentence 3 changes the present tense to the past tense correctly and is the right option.
